verses.sanskrit: जनमेजय उवाच । एवं ते मत्स्यनगरे प्रच्छन्नाः कुरुनन्दनाः । अत ऊर्ध्वं महावीर्याः किमकुर्वत वै द्विज ॥१॥
verses.english: Janamejaya said O twice-born one, living thus disguised in the city of the Matsyas what did the Kuru's sons of exceeding might do.

verses.sanskrit: वैशम्पायन उवाच । एवं मत्स्यस्य नगरे प्रच्छन्नाः कुरुनन्दनाः । आराधयन्तो राजानं यदकुर्वत तच्छृणु ॥२॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Hear, what the descendants of Kuru did living thus disguised in the city of the Matsyas and serving the king thereof.

verses.sanskrit: तृणबिन्दुप्रसादाच्च धर्मस्य च महात्मनः । अज्ञातवासमेवं तु विराटनगरेऽवसन् ॥३॥
verses.english: By the grace of the ascetic Trinabindu and of the high-souled Dharma they began to live incognito in the city of Virata.

verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिरः सभास्तारो मत्स्यानामभवत् प्रियः । तथैव च विराटस्य सपुत्रस्य विशाम्पते ॥४॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira as a courtier made himself a favorite to Virata and his son, as well as to all the Matsyas, O lord of people.

verses.sanskrit: स ह्यक्षहृदयज्ञस्तान् क्रीडयामास पाण्डवः । अक्षवत्यां यथाकामं सूत्रबद्धानिव द्विजान् ॥५॥
verses.english: Well versed in the mysteries of the dice he caused him to play at dice in the dice-hall in accordance with his pleasure like the birds bound by the string.

verses.sanskrit: अज्ञातं च विराटस्य विजित्य वसु धर्मराट् । भ्रातृभ्यः पुरुषव्याघ्रो यथार्हं संप्रयच्छति ॥६॥
verses.english: That best of men, the king of justice (Yudhishthira) having won the wealth of Virata duly distributed it without the knowledge of the monarch among his brothers.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनोऽपि मांसानि भक्ष्याणि विविधानि च । अतिसृष्टानि मत्स्येन विक्रीणीते युधिष्ठिरे ॥७॥
verses.english: Bhimsena also sold to Yudhishthira, the meat and the viands of various sorts which were given by the king of the Matsyas.

verses.sanskrit: वासांसि परिजीर्णानि लब्धान्यन्तःपुरेऽर्जुनः । विक्रीणानश्च सर्वेभ्यः पाण्डवेभ्यः प्रयच्छति ॥८॥
verses.english: Arjuna parted with the worn out clothes by sale, which he obtained from women's quarters, to the other sons of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: सहदेवोऽपि गोपानां वेषमास्थाय पाण्डवः । दधि क्षीरं घृतं चैव पाण्डवेभ्यः प्रयच्छति ॥९॥
verses.english: Sahadeva also, who had assumed the dress of a cow-herd, distributed to them curds, milk and clarified butter.

verses.sanskrit: नकुलोऽपि धनं लब्ध्वा कृते कर्मणि वाजिनाम् । तुष्टे तस्मिन्नरपतौ पाण्डवेभ्यः प्रयच्छति ॥१०॥
verses.english: Nakula also gave the wealth to his brothers which he acquired from the king who was satisfied with him for his tending the horses.

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णा तु सर्वान् भर्तॄंस्तान्निरीक्षन्ती तपस्विनी । यथा पुनरविज्ञाता तथा चरति भामिनी ॥११॥
verses.english: In the form of ascetic and very charmful draupadi served their husband, so nobody can identify their reality.

verses.sanskrit: एवं सम्पादयन्तस्ते तदाऽन्योन्यं महारथाः । विराटनगरे चेरुः पुनर्गर्भधृता इव ॥१२॥
verses.english: They, the mighty warriors, then looking after the interest of one another, lived in the city of Virata in such a manner, as if they were once more in the house of their mother.

verses.sanskrit: साशङ्का धार्तराष्ट्रस्य भयात् पाण्डुसुतास्तदा । प्रेक्षमाणास्तदा कृष्णामूषुश्छन्ना नराधिप ॥१३॥
verses.english: Then the sons of Pandu, the lords of men, appending evil from the sons of Dhritarashtra, continued to live there in disguise keeping vigilant eyes upon their wife Krishna.
verses.bhavadeepa: एवमिति । सम्पादयन्तोऽन्योन्यमाराधयन्तः गर्भधृता इव प्रच्छन्नत्वेन सेवाश्रमेण च दुःखिता इत्यर्थः ॥१२॥

verses.sanskrit: अथ मासे चतुर्थे तु ब्रह्मणः सुमहोत्सवः । आसीत् समृद्धो मत्स्येषु पुरुषाणां सुसंमतः ॥१४॥
verses.english: Then in the fourth month there happened a great festival, in honor of the divine Brahma, slender in form and highly valued by people, in the city of the Matsya's.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र मल्लाः समापेतुर्दिग्भ्यो राजन् सहस्रशः । समाजे ब्रह्मणो राजन् यथा पशुपतेरिव ॥१५॥
verses.english: 0 king, there came, by thousands, wrestlers from all quarters in that field of festivity in honour of the divine Brahma, as also on the occasion of a festival held in honor of Shiva.
verses.bhavadeepa: ब्रह्मणः उत्सवः शरदि नवधान्योत्पत्तौ सर्वैः क्रियते स च देशविशेषे प्रसिद्धः ॥१४॥

verses.sanskrit: महाकाया महावीर्याः कालखञ्जा इवासुराः । वीर्योन्मत्ता वलोदग्रा राज्ञा समभिपूजिताः ॥१६॥
verses.english: They were of colossal forms and of exceeding might, like the demons named Kalakhanjas; they were maddened with their latent power; furious with their prowess and highly honored by the king.
verses.bhavadeepa: यथा ब्रह्मणः समाजे ब्रह्मलोके कैलासे वा पशुपतेः समाजे इव मत्स्येषु समापेतुरिति सम्बन्धः ॥१५॥

verses.sanskrit: सिंहस्कन्धकटिग्रीवाः स्ववदाता मनस्विनः । असकृल्लब्धलक्षास्ते रङ्गे पार्थिवसन्निधौ ॥१७॥
verses.english: Their shoulders, waists and necks were like those of lions, their bodies were free from dirt, and their hearts were large. Many times before they achieved success in the lists in the very august presence of the king.

verses.sanskrit: तेषामेको महानासीत् सर्वमल्लानथाह्वयत् । आवल्गमानं तं रङ्गे नोपतिष्ठति कश्चन ॥१८॥
verses.english: Amongst them there was one who was the greatest of all and challenged all other combatants to a wrestle; there was none that ventured to encounter him as he strided over in the arena.
verses.bhavadeepa: स्ववदाताः अत्यन्तनिर्मलाः मनस्विनः प्रीतमनसः लब्धलक्षाः प्राप्तविजयाः ॥१७॥

verses.sanskrit: यदा सर्वे विमनसस्ते मल्ला हतचेतसः । अथ सूदेन तं मल्लं योधयामास मत्स्यराट् ॥१९॥
verses.english: When all the wrestlers stood stupefied and dejected in spirit then the king of the Matsyas made him fight with his cook.

verses.sanskrit: नोद्यमानस्तदा भीमो दुःखेनैवाकरोन्मतिम् । न हि शक्नोति विवृते प्रत्याख्यातुं नराधिपम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: Impelled by the king, Bhima made up his mind with reluctance, for it was not in his power to openly disobey the royal mandate.

verses.sanskrit: ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रः शार्दूलशिथिलश्चरन् । प्रविवेश महारङ्गं विराटमभिपूजयन् ॥२१॥
verses.english: Then that the best of men, having worshipped the king Virata, entered the spacious arena with listless steps like those of a lion.
verses.bhavadeepa: दुःखेनैव पारतन्त्र्यात् प्राकट्यभयाद्वा दुःखं न तु भङ्गभयात् । विवृते प्रकाशे ॥२०॥

verses.sanskrit: बबन्ध कक्षां कौन्तेयस्ततः संहर्षयन् जनम् । ततस्तु वृत्रसङ्काशं भीमो मल्लं समाह्वयत् ॥२२॥
verses.english: Then Bhima, the son of Kunti, girded up his lions and caused the delight of the spectators. There he summoned the wrestler of distinguished prowess named Jimuta resembling Vritra himself. were

verses.sanskrit: जीमूतं नाम तं तत्र मल्लं प्रख्यातविक्रमम् । तावुभौ सुमहोत्साहावुभौ भीमपराक्रमौ ॥२३॥
verses.english: Both of them were of exceeding energy and of terrible prowess, and they both were like a couple of infuriated elephants of gigantic form each being sixty years old. Then those two best of men became engaged in hand-tohand fight.
verses.bhavadeepa: कक्षां परिकरम् । कच्छामिति पाठेऽपि स एवार्थः । यद्वा कक्षां रज्जुं रज्ज्वा पाटनभयान्मल्लैरङ्गुल्यो बध्यन्त इति प्रसिद्धेरङ्गुलीर्बध्वेत्यर्थः ॥२२॥

verses.sanskrit: मत्ताविव महाकायौ वारणौ षष्टिहायनौ । ततस्तौ नरशार्दूलौ बाहुयुद्धं समीयतुः ॥२४॥
वीरौ परमसंहृष्टावन्योन्यजयकाङ्क्षिणौ । आसीत् सुभीमः संपातो वज्रपर्वतयोरिव ॥२५॥
verses.english: Those two heroic combatants exceedingly cheerful, each being desirous of gaining victory over the other; exceedingly terrible was the encounter between them, just like the clash of the thunderbolt against the mountain.

verses.sanskrit: उभौ परमसंहृष्टौ बलेनातिबलावुभौ । अन्योन्यस्यान्तरं प्रेप्सू परस्परजयैषिणौ ॥२६॥
verses.english: Both of them were exceedingly powerful and were highly pleased with each other's strength; each of them was desirous of winning the victory over the other and was vigilant to take advantage of his rival's lapse.

verses.sanskrit: उभौ परमसंहृष्टौ मत्ताविव महागजौ । कृतप्रतिकृतैश्चित्रैर्बाहुभिश्च सुसङ्कटैः । सन्निपातावधूतैश्च प्रमाथोन्मथनैस्तथा ॥२७॥
verses.english: Both of them were exceedingly delighted and resembled a couple of infuriated elephants of huge forms; and various were the manners of their attack and defence shown by means of their clenched fists.

verses.sanskrit: क्षेपणैर्मुष्टिभिश्चैव वराहोद्धूतनिःस्वनैः । तलैर्वज्रनिपातैश्च प्रसृष्टाभिस्तथैव च ॥२८॥
verses.english: They fought in a manner that each dashed against the other, threw his rival far off his stand, each crushed the other down, and pressed him hard on the ground, each showing the other off exchanged blows, and each whirled the other round with his head downward and threw him away with a loud noise.
verses.bhavadeepa: कृतं क्वचिद्देशे निपीडनम् । प्रतिकृतं तस्य मोचनम् । सुसंकटैर्मुष्टिग्रहणेन कृशीकृतैः । सकण्टकैरिति पाठे सकवचैः सकिणैर्वा ‘कण्टको बाहुचरणकवचे कठिने किणे’ इति विश्वः । सन्निपातोऽङ्गसङ्घट्टनम् अवधूतं तेनैव दूरीकरणं । प्रमाथादय उक्ता मल्लशास्त्रे - ‘निपात्य पेषणं भूमौ प्रमाथ इति कथ्यते । यत्तूत्थायाङ्गमथनं तदुन्मथनमुच्यते’ ॥२७॥

verses.sanskrit: शलाकानखपातैश्च पादोद्धूतैश्च दारुणैः । जानुभिश्चाश्मनिर्घोषैः शिरोभिश्चावघट्ट‌नैः ॥२९॥
verses.english: With their palms each gave a good slap to the other, striking as hard as the thunder bolt and with outstretched fingers they slapped each other. They thrust spear like nails into each other's person; each gave violent kicks to the other.

verses.sanskrit: तद्युद्धमभवद्धोरमशस्त्रं बाहुतेजसा । बलप्राणेन शूराणां समाजोत्सवसन्निधौ ॥३०॥
verses.english: They struck knee against knee, dashed head against head, producing the crash of one stone against another. That was the furious combat without weapons, sustained chiefly by the might of their arms.

verses.sanskrit: अरज्यत जनः सर्वः सोत्कृष्टनिनदोत्थितः । बालनोः संयुगे राजन् वृत्रवासवयोरिव ॥३१॥
verses.bhavadeepa: अशस्त्रं निन्द्यम् यथोक्तं तत्रैव - ‘बाहुयुद्धं हि मल्लानामशस्त्रमृषिभिः स्मृतम् । मृतस्य तस्य न स्वर्गो यशो नेहापि विद्यते’ इति । बलप्राणेन बलेन शारीरबणेन प्राणेन मानसबलेन च ॥३०॥

verses.sanskrit: प्रकर्षणाकर्षणयोरभ्याकर्षविकर्षणैः । आकर्षतुरथान्योन्यं जानुभिश्चापि जघ्नतुः ॥३२॥
ततः शब्देन महता भर्त्सयन्तौ परस्परम् । व्यूढोरस्कौ दीर्घभुजौ नियुद्धकुशलावुभौ । बाहुभिः समसज्जेतामायसैः परिघैरिव ॥३३॥
verses.english: Then they both of expansive chest, and long arms, and expert in wrestling began to fight with their arms resembling huge bolts of iron.

verses.sanskrit: चकर्ष दोर्ज्यामुत्पात्य भीमो मल्लममित्रहा । निनदन्तमभिक्रोशन् शार्दूल इव वारणम् ॥३४॥
verses.english: Bhima, the slayer of enemies, seized, with a big seized, his vociferous rival wrestler by the arms and drew him near even as the lion seizes the elephant.

verses.sanskrit: समुद्यम्य महाबाहुर्भ्रामयामास वीर्यवान् । ततो मल्लाश्च मत्स्याश्च विस्मयं चक्रिरे परम् ॥३५॥
verses.english: Then the mighty-armed Bhima of great prowess raised him up and began to whirl him round; then all the athlete and the people of the Matsya's, who had assembled on the occasion, were greatly astonished.

verses.sanskrit: भ्रामयित्त्वा शतगुणं गतसत्त्वमचेतनम् । प्रत्यर्पिषन्महाबाहुर्मल्लं भुवि वृकोदरः ॥३६॥
verses.english: Then having whirled him round and round a hundred times, the mighty armed Vrikodara inade him utterly insensible and threw him down lifeless on the ground.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन् विनिहते वीरे जीमूते लोकविश्रुते । विराटः परमं हर्षमगच्छद्बान्धवैः सह ॥३७॥
verses.english: That distinguished athlete Jimuta being slain, Virata and his friends were exceedingly delighted.

verses.sanskrit: प्रहर्षात् प्रददौ वित्तं बहु राजा महामनाः । बल्लवाय महारङ्गे यथा वैश्रवणस्तथा ॥३८॥
verses.english: In his great joy the high-minded king gave away to Ballava plenty of riches in the shape of a reward on the very field of combat with as much liberality as that of Kubera.

verses.sanskrit: एवं स सुबहून् मल्लान् पुरुषांश्च महाबलान् । विनिघ्नन् मत्स्यराजस्य प्रीतिमाहरदुत्तमाम् ॥३९॥
verses.english: Having thus slain numerous athletes and many other persons of great strength he received the great favour of the king of the Matsya's.

verses.sanskrit: यदास्य तुल्यः पुरुषो न कश्चित्तत्र विद्यते । ततो व्याघ्रैश्च सिंहैश्च द्विरदैश्चाप्ययोधयत् ॥४०॥
verses.english: When there was found no one such as to stand equal to him the king made him fight with tigers and lions and elephants.

verses.sanskrit: पुनरन्तःपुरगतः स्त्रीणां मध्ये वृकोदरः । योध्यते स विराटेन सिंहैर्मत्तैर्महाबलैः ॥४१॥
verses.english: Again the king made Vrikodara fight with furious lions of exceeding strength in the assembly of the ladies of the harem.

verses.sanskrit: बीभत्सुरपि गीतेन स्वनृत्येन च पाण्डवः । विराटं तोषयामास सर्वाश्चान्तःपुरस्त्रियः ॥४२॥
verses.english: Bibhatsu, the son of Pandu, pleased Virata and all the ladies of the harem by singing and dancing.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वैर्विनीतैर्जवनैस्तत्र तत्र समागतैः । तोषयामास राजानं नकुलो नृपसत्तमम् ॥४३॥
verses.english: Nakula pleased the king, the best of kings by showing him the fast-going and well-trained horses and the king, pleased gave him a plenty of money as a reward.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मै प्रदेयं प्रायच्छत् प्रीतो राजा धनं बहु । विनीतान् वृषभान् दृष्ट्वा सहदेवस्य चाभितः । धनं ददौ वहुविधं विराटः पुरुषर्षभः ॥४४॥
verses.english: Beholding a herd of well-trained bullocks around Sahadeva, Virata the best of men, gave him wealth of various kinds.

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपदी प्रेक्ष्य तान्सर्वान् क्लिश्यमानान्महारथान् । नातिप्रीतमना राजन्निःश्वासपरमाऽभवत् ॥४५॥
verses.english: O king, beholding all these mighty warriors suffer pain, Draupadi felt herself dejected in mind and had recourse to constant sighs.

verses.sanskrit: एवं ते न्यवसंस्तत्र प्रच्छन्नाः पुरुषर्षभाः । कर्माणि तस्य कुर्वाणा विराटनृपतेस्तदा ॥४६॥
verses.english: Those best among men began to live there in disguise rendering services to the king Virata.
